transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I've been struggling a lot with constant fidgeting and finding it really difficult to just sit still. It feels like I always need to be tapping my hands or moving my feet, and it's becoming really hard to manage.
Have you also had trouble focusing or felt the need to blurt out answers before questions are finished?

No, I don't really have trouble focusing on things, and I don't think I blurt out answers before people finish speaking. For me, it's really just the physical restlessness and that constant need to keep moving.
When did these symptoms of restlessness and fidgeting first start, and have they been present since childhood?

I've been struggling with this really intensely for about two years and one month now. However, looking back, it actually first started when I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12. It just seems to have become much more of a problem recently.
How is this restlessness affecting your daily life, such as at work, in relationships, or during social situations?

To be honest, I'm not quite sure how to describe the exact impact it has. I haven't really thought about how it affects my work or relationships specifically, it's just a constant uncomfortable feeling I have to deal with.
Can you think of any specific situations—like during meetings, while driving, or when trying to relax—where the need to move has caused you distress or made it hard to function?

It's definitely worst during things like long meetings or quiet moments when I'm expected to sit still. In those situations, I constantly feel restless and find myself fidgeting, tapping my hands or feet, or squirming in my seat. It makes it really hard to just sit through them without feeling extremely uncomfortable.
Do you ever feel an inner sense of restlessness or urge to move even when you're not fidgeting outwardly, or is the discomfort only present when you're physically still?

Yes, absolutely. I frequently feel a deep inner sense of restlessness and a constant urge to move, even when I am trying my best to remain still. That discomfort is almost always there internally, and it usually ends up showing outwardly through my constant fidgeting, tapping, and squirming.
Have these symptoms of inner restlessness and physical fidgeting been present in most situations—like at work, at home, or during leisure time—for more than six months?

Yes, absolutely. I experience both the physical fidgeting and that inner restlessness in almost every setting, whether I'm at work, at home, or just trying to relax during my free time. It has definitely been going on for much longer than six months, as it's been a constant issue for over two years now.
Have you ever had periods of prolonged, purposeless movements—like rocking, hand-wringing, or other repetitive actions—that are different from typical fidgeting?
No, I don't think I experience anything like that. I have never had those types of repetitive movements like rocking or hand-wringing. For me, it is really just the usual tapping and squirming.

The absence of prominent inattention rules out combined and inattentive presentations, while the chronicity and developmental onset support ADHD over other conditions like anxiety or movement disorders. No new symptoms suggest an alternative diagnosis.
